Classify a pedon under the French soil classification (CPCS 1967)

Source: R/key-cpcs1967.R
classify_cpcs1967.Rd

Keys a PedonRecord through the twelve classes of the French soil classification of 1967 (Commission de Pedologie et de Cartographie des Sols). Experimental: this release keys the classes (sols mineraux bruts, sols peu evolues, vertisols, andosols, sols calcimagnesiques, sols isohumiques, sols brunifies, sols podzolises, sols a sesquioxydes de fer et manganese, sols ferrallitiques, sols hydromorphes, sols sodiques), their 35 sub-classes, the climatic ones read from site$koppen_climate, else the USDA soil temperature and moisture regimes, else the latitude (with no climate, the non-climatic or temperate sub-class), their 101 groups and their 276 subgroups (a group or subgroup the data cannot decide leaves the name provisional; when no group of a sub-class, or no subgroup of a group, fits, the name stops at the level above, and none is invented). The names are French, as the text writes them, in name and in levels$name_native; a subgroup named by an adjective is shown after its group ("Rankers, a mor"), one the text names in full stands alone, and the other subgroups whose tests pass are noted in the trace as intergrades.

Usage

classify_cpcs1967(
  pedon,
  rules = NULL,
  on_missing = c("warn", "silent", "error"),
  gapfill = FALSE
)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

rules

Optional pre-loaded rule set (load_rules("cpcs1967")).

on_missing

One of "warn" (default), "silent", "error".

gapfill

Opt-in within-pedon gap-fill, as in classify_usda.

Value

A ClassificationResult with system_id "cpcs1967", the deepest class assigned in name, the class in rsg_or_order, the classes of each level in levels (with name_native), the key trace, and provisional_because (classes before the assigned one that could not be decided).

Details

The CPCS gives no key. soilKey keys the classes in an order built from the text's own statements of precedence: raw mineral soils, vertisols, sodic soils, andosols, podzolised, ferrallitic and sesquioxide soils, hydromorphic soils, weakly developed soils, isohumic soils, calcimagnesic soils, and the brunified soils last; a peat is a hydromorphic soil, whatever lies under it. Every threshold of the text is in depths from the top of the first mineral horizon.

The key reads the old French horizon notation (Aoo, Ao, A1, A2, A3, (B), B, Bh, Bfe, Bt, C, Cca, G, g, R, a Roman numeral for a change of parent material), declared with site$designation_system = "cpcs" or recognised by its symbols, beside the FAO letters; where a profile has no designations, soilKey's diagnostic horizons stand in. From the horizons it reads organic carbon and nitrogen, texture, pH, the CEC and the exchangeable bases, carbonate and gypsum, the EC of the saturated paste, Ki (sio2_sulfuric_pct, al2o3_sulfuric_pct), the andic properties, moist and dry Munsell colours, mottles, slickensides, cracks, structure and consistence, clay films, coarse fragments, the sand minerals, the fibre content of peat, ice (ice_pct, ice_form), and the recorded origin of the layers; from the site the climate, the soil temperature regime, the parent material, recorded erosion, the water table, the elevation, patterned ground (patterned_ground) and the humus form (humus_form); for some subgroups also active carbonate (caco3_active_pct), the coarse and fine sand (coarse_sand_pct, fine_sand_pct) and gibbsite (gibbsite_pct). The choices where the text is silent are listed in system.file("rules", "cpcs1967", "readings.yaml", package = "soilKey").

References

Commission de Pedologie et de Cartographie des Sols (1967). Classification des sols. ENSA, Grignon. Digitised by the AFES (2011).

See also

make_cpcs1967_example, soilkey_systems.

Examples

res <- classify_cpcs1967(make_cpcs1967_example("ferrallitic"), on_missing = "silent")
res$name
#> [1] "Sols ferrallitiques moyennement désaturés en (B) typiques, Faiblement appauvri"
res$levels
#>        level  code
#> 1    classes     X
#> 2 subclasses   X-2
#> 3     groups  X/21
#> 4  subgroups X/216
#>                                                                             name
#> 1                                                            Sols ferrallitiques
#> 2                               Sols ferrallitiques moyennement désaturés en (B)
#> 3                      Sols ferrallitiques moyennement désaturés en (B) typiques
#> 4 Sols ferrallitiques moyennement désaturés en (B) typiques, Faiblement appauvri
#>                                                                      name_native
#> 1                                                            Sols ferrallitiques
#> 2                               Sols ferrallitiques moyennement désaturés en (B)
#> 3                      Sols ferrallitiques moyennement désaturés en (B) typiques
#> 4 Sols ferrallitiques moyennement désaturés en (B) typiques, Faiblement appauvri
